response.message:
I've drawn an AWS sketch where a PR webhook flows through API Gateway into SQS and a review Lambda. The Lambda uses a read-only token to fetch only the diff and the changed files, asks Bedrock for an analysis, and saves draft comments tied to changed lines in DynamoDB. It never checks out, runs, pushes or merges anything. Nothing has been deployed, and no region or account access has been approved.

**First local test:** we replay a synthetic PR webhook and diff through the flow, with a scripted model reply standing in for Bedrock. That shows the plumbing, line mapping and fail-closed checks work. It doesn't show anything about real review quality, model access, IAM or quotas. Those need a separate run against a real Bedrock model with a set of known example PRs.

The generator can't build this review pipeline yet, so it's still engineering work. I haven't shrunk the design down to storage to get around that.

Should the draft comments go back to the PR automatically as a pending review, or wait for a person to approve each one before anything is written to the repository?

proposal.title: AWS PR review assistant – first end-to-end sketch
proposal.body: Scope: review one synthetic PR from an existing repository: authorized diff retrieval, AI analysis, and line-linked draft comments. Read-only on the repository; no push, merge or code execution. Assumptions: the repo host supports signed webhooks and a read-only app token; Bedrock model and region not yet selected; whether comments get posted back is still undecided. The custom ingest and review components aren't covered by the native generator yet and still need engineering.

data.label: Existing Git repository host
data.description: Existing repository with synthetic PR. Sends signed PR webhook; serves diff and file contents to a read-only, repo-scoped token. Never modified.

data.label: PR webhook endpoint
data.description: Receives PR events. A small validator checks the webhook signature and allowed repository, then enqueues. Rejects unknown repos.

data.label: Review job queue
data.description: Buffers review jobs keyed by repo+PR+head commit SHA for idempotent processing.

data.label: Failed review jobs
data.description: Holds jobs that failed repeatedly, for operator inspection.

data.label: PR review worker
data.description: Fetches only the authorized diff and relevant changed files (size-bounded), treats code as untrusted text and never executes it. Builds the prompt, calls the model, validates that each comment maps to a changed line, and stores drafts. No push or merge permissions.

data.label: Read-only repo credential
data.description: Stores the read-only repo token, readable only by the worker role. The value never appears in the diagram.

data.label: Review model
data.description: Foundation model invoked via Converse. Model ID, access, region and quotas still need verification. Mocked in local tests.

data.label: Draft review comments
data.description: Stores line-linked draft comments per PR/head SHA (file, line, side, text, model ID). Uses conditional writes for idempotency.

data.label: Human code reviewer
data.description: Reviews the drafts. Whether they get posted to the PR is an open decision.

data.label: Logs and metrics
data.description: Worker logs (no source code bodies), latency, errors and a DLQ depth alarm.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Prevents changes to the repository and blocks code-execution or prompt-injection attacks through untrusted code.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Retrieve only the authorized diff and relevant files… Never push, merge or execute repository code."
requirementDrafts.statement: The system shall only read the authorized PR diff and relevant changed files. It shall never push, merge, check out or execute repository code.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Comments on lines outside the diff mislead reviewers and can fail when posted.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "draft review comments linked to changed lines"
requirementDrafts.statement: Every draft comment shall reference a file and a line that exists in the PR diff. Comments that can't be mapped to a changed line shall be rejected.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Mocked replies prove the plumbing works but say nothing about review quality, model access or quotas.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation"
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: model quality shall be checked against the real Bedrock model on a labelled set of synthetic PRs, kept separate from mocked local tests.

response.message: The emulation shows no failed checks. It's blocked because none of our eight AWS components have a native generator contract yet: the webhook endpoint, queue, DLQ, review worker, secret, drafts table, and the existing repo and Bedrock references all need implementation or an import plan. To answer the checker's question: no supported contract fits without changing the scope. The async word-count pipeline starts from S3 uploads, and bedrock-summary only handles direct text summaries, so forcing either one onto this design would quietly drop the webhook, read-only diff retrieval and line-linked drafts. That makes this product engineering work, and this artifact digest is the reproducer: a typed "pr-review" contract covering the webhook signature check, an SQS worker with a scoped Secrets Manager read, Bedrock Converse calls and conditional DynamoDB writes. I haven't changed the diagram because no edit to it can fill that gap. So let's settle the decision that defines that contract's permissions: should the system only ever store drafts for a person to read, or will a reviewer later approve drafts so they get posted to the PR?
